summary: Iowa is one of the cleaner states for the roof rat. The Dangerous Wild Animals law (Iowa Code ch. 717F) is a closed list — big cats, bears, wolves, primates, crocodilians, venomous snakes — that includes NO rodents, and DNR jurisdiction (ch. 481A) covers native wildlife and wild releases, not an indoor captive-bred pet. So keeping, breeding, and selling/giving are legal at the state level. Two administrative touchpoints: a pet-shop/dealer license (IDALS) only kicks in above $500/yr OR 6+ animals/yr in sales, and importing needs a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (Iowa's prohibited-rodent import list — the monkeypox seven — does NOT include Rattus). Never release one.

keep.why: Iowa Code §717F.1 defines 'dangerous wild animal' as a closed list of enumerated families/orders (Canidae, Felidae, Ursidae, Rhinocerotidae, Proboscidea, Primates, Crocodilia, venomous snakes/lizards) — order Rodentia is absent. DNR (ch. 481A) regulates native wildlife and wild introductions, not a captive-bred indoor pet rodent. No state possession permit applies.
keep.governing_law: Iowa Code §717F.1 (dangerous wild animal — no rodents); Iowa Code §481A.47 (native wildlife / wild introduction).

breed.why: ch. 717F doesn't cover rodents and §481A.47 governs only wild introductions, not closed-colony captive breeding. IDALS Animal Welfare rules (IAC 21 ch. 67) require a pet-shop/dealer license only above the thresholds ($500/yr OR 6+ animals/yr); hobby breeding below that is unregulated.

sell_give.why: No Iowa law prohibits selling/giving captive-bred rodents not on the ch. 717F list. Commercial sale above $500/yr OR 6+ animals/yr makes you a 'pet shop' needing an IDALS license (IAC 21-67); free adoption and small sales are exempt.
sell_give.governing_law: IAC 21-67.1 (pet-shop definition + thresholds); Iowa Code ch. 162.

transport.why: Intrastate transport is unregulated. IMPORT requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection under IAC 21-65; Iowa's prohibited-rodent import list (prairie dogs, Gambian rats, dormice, etc. — the 2003 monkeypox seven) does NOT include Rattus rattus. Confirm the pet-rodent CVI application with IDALS. Never release a roof rat.
transport.governing_law: IAC 21-65.3 (import CVI + prohibited-rodent list, Rattus absent).

restrictions.summary: An IDALS pet-shop/dealer license is required only if you sell/breed above the thresholds ($500/yr OR 6+ animals/yr); below that, hobby breeding and free adoption need no license.
steps: Stay under the IAC 21-67 thresholds, or obtain an IDALS pet-shop license
restrictions.where_to_file: Iowa Dept of Agriculture & Land Stewardship (Animal Welfare)

restrictions.summary: Importing a pet rat into Iowa requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (IAC 21-65). Rattus is not on Iowa's prohibited-import rodent list. No CVI for in-state movement; never release.
